summary: TeamNest.ai AI Conversation Mode Phase 2 POLISH tested on backend + web + mobile. Backend: 9/9 pytest passed — route-preview returns {score, decision, threshold, reasons} with correct decisions ('make it shorter'->ai 0.99, 'thanks team...'->chat 0.4, threshold override lowers/raises decision as expected). ai-session now exposes context_summary + assistant_label. AI employee session hook verified end-to-end via '@cmo' catalog mention: session.assistant_id becomes 'employee:cmo' and untagged follow-up 'make it shorter' auto-routes to AI CMO (ai-cmo sender, employee_key=cmo) — NOT to generic @ai. Multi-assistant switch banner ('Active AI changed from @AI to @ai') verified in messages after switching between @cmo -> @ai. save-to-role no longer 500s (returns proposed>=0). Web: /ai-memory admin 'Workspace defaults' shows preview-input + preview-result + preview-decision='AI'. Mobile: /settings/ai-conversation admin shows preview-input + preview-result 'Would route to: AI conf 0.99' with correct badge. Memory-peek UI code is correctly gated on aiSession.active && aiSession.context_summary — code review verified selectors + bindings; not exercised end-to-end in a chat where the session had a populated context_summary in this run (rolling summary refresh requires 4+ AI turns AND the LLM background task to finish; the ai-session shape now includes the field so the UI will render as soon as it lands).

parity_issues.issue: Behaviour identical (both platforms show AI/Ask/Team chat badge + confidence).

action_items: MINOR: assistant_label for catalog AI employees currently resolves to '@AI' (from ai_employee_dispatcher.py:318: `f"@{(emp.get('name') or 'AI').split(' ')[0]}"` where emp.name='AI CMO' -> first token 'AI'). This makes CMO/Sales/Paralegal all render as '@AI' — indistinguishable from the base @ai assistant and from each other. Review request expected label like '@Cmo'. Suggest: use `emp.get('command')` (e.g. 'AI CMO') minus the 'AI ' prefix, or use employee_key.title() — e.g. `f"@{employee_key.capitalize()}"` -> '@Cmo'. Same concern in ai_employee_deploy_dispatcher.py (deploy path currently already uses the deployed handle in labels — validate). This also affects the switch banner text: currently posts 'Active AI changed from @AI to @ai' which is confusing (case-only difference).

OPTIONAL: The memory-peek toggle only renders when aiSession.context_summary is populated AND session is active — verified via code review. End-to-end UI trigger requires a chat with 4+ AI turns and the background _refresh_conversation_summary task to complete. Main agent may want to add a dev/QA affordance to force-populate context_summary or a small debug script (e.g. a POST /api/chats/{id}/ai-session/refresh-summary) so testers can exercise the UI without waiting for the rolling summary cadence.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/ai_conversation.py:14-27 — _public_session now correctly exposes assistant_label + context_summary (Feature A). LGTM.

routes/ai_conversation.py:170-188 — /ai-conversation/route-preview: builds a synthetic session with last_activity_at=now (to satisfy 'very_recent' reason) and uses effective settings when no threshold passed. Correctly requires auth (require_user) but not admin — matches the spec 'Available to any authenticated user'. LGTM.

routes/ai_conversation.py:222-253 (save-to-role) — new_id + now_iso are now used in the proposed>0 path via top-level import (line 8: `from deps import ... new_id, now_iso ...`); regression fix verified. 200 response on real content-rich chat.

services/ai_employee_dispatcher.py:314-329 — Correctly calls both note_active_assistant() and start_or_refresh_session() so the session pointer moves to 'employee:<key>' AND the switch banner is posted when the assistant changes. Fire-and-forget wrapper via try/except so any DB error doesn't block the employee reply. LGTM apart from the label derivation bug noted above.
services/ai_employee_deploy_dispatcher.py:120-135 — Same pattern for deployed employees using 'deploy:<handle>'. Not exercised in this run (no deployed employees in preview env).

success_rate.frontend: 100% for verified surfaces (web B live-preview + mobile B live-preview confirmed on real UI; web/mobile A memory-peek code + selectors confirmed by review, gated on runtime context_summary population)

test_credentials: sam@funasia.net / Perfect$2008 used (super admin, unlimited credits, has AI employees available).
seed_data_creation: Two throwaway group chats created and best-effort cleared via /clear: TEST_iter112_polish (rolling-summary + save-to-role) and TEST_iter112_C (feature C — @cmo + follow-up + @ai switch). A handful of ai_conversation_sessions rows left in DB (safe to keep).
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 3 polish features are functionally correct on backend + Feature B UI (web + mobile) is fully exercised. The one behavioural nit: catalog AI employees all get assistant_label='@AI' because the label is derived from the FIRST token of emp['name']='AI XYZ'. Recommend main agent switch to `emp['name'].replace('AI ','')` or `employee_key.title()`. Web/mobile memory-peek UI (Feature A) is code-review clean and the API now serves context_summary/assistant_label — end-to-end UI verification needs an existing chat with an active session + populated context_summary (rolling summary requires >=4 AI turns and the background task).
rca of the issue: Assistant-label bug RCA: `services/ai_employee_dispatcher.py:318` computes `label = f"@{(emp.get('name') or 'AI').split(' ')[0]}"` — since all catalog employees have name starting with 'AI ' (AI CMO / AI Sales / AI Paralegal), split(' ')[0] always returns 'AI'. Fix: use `emp['name'].replace('AI ','',1)` or `employee_key.capitalize()` to yield '@Cmo' / '@Sales' / '@Paralegal' as the spec expects.
